mechanics.mechanic: Open by defining the subject broadly, then narrow it into the specific process, applications, and outcomes the discussion will cover. This gives the audience both a conceptual frame and a practical reason to continue.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use at the beginning of an educational piece when the topic has multiple meanings, mechanisms, or use cases.
mechanics.avoid: Do not promise every possible angle or introduce technical detail before clarifying the central subject.

mechanics.mechanic: Identify the audience’s likely first assumption, briefly challenge it, and signal that the explanation will show why the assumption is incomplete.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use when the topic produces a common but oversimplified reaction that could interfere with later learning.
mechanics.avoid: Do not frame disagreement as a personal correction or make a broad claim without explaining the conditions under which the opposite may occur.

mechanics.mechanic: Introduce one simple organizing distinction early, such as two compartments, stages, or interacting systems, and repeatedly use it to structure later explanations.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use when a complex subject becomes easier to understand through a stable conceptual contrast.
mechanics.avoid: Do not add multiple competing frameworks before the first one is established.

mechanics.function: Sequencing mechanism from input to outcome
mechanics.mechanic: Explain a causal pathway in ordered stages: stimulus, detection, relay, control center, bodily response, and observable consequence. Translate specialized components into plain-language roles as they appear.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use for biology, technology, policy, or any subject where understanding depends on how an effect is produced rather than merely knowing that it occurs.
mechanics.avoid: Do not overload the sequence with names that do not contribute to the causal explanation.

mechanics.function: Using counterintuitive examples to test the model
mechanics.mechanic: Present a scenario in which the obvious action appears to produce one result, then show how the underlying system produces a different result. Use the contrast to reinforce the governing model.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use after introducing a mechanism, especially when the system responds indirectly or through feedback.
mechanics.avoid: Do not use surprising examples that cannot be connected back to the model or that encourage unsafe experimentation.

mechanics.mechanic: Distinguish a static condition from the transition into, through, and out of that condition. Explain that timing, sequencing, repetition, or contrast may determine the outcome more than the endpoint alone.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use when results depend on exposure dynamics, adaptation, feedback, or repeated cycles.
mechanics.avoid: Do not imply that one observed protocol is universally optimal or that a single variable explains the full effect.

mechanics.mechanic: Move from a broad finding to study context, population, comparison, measurement, and possible confounders. Clarify whether the evidence is observational, experimental, mechanistic, or extrapolated.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use when discussing research findings that may otherwise sound more definitive than the design supports.
mechanics.avoid: Do not convert association into causation, hide sample limitations, or use numerical precision to create unwarranted certainty.

mechanics.mechanic: Present practical guidance as a set of controllable variables, then explain how intensity, duration, frequency, access, tolerance, and safety alter the choice. Offer lower-cost or more accessible alternatives while distinguishing them from the studied setup.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use when translating research into real-world action without pretending that all substitutes are equivalent.
mechanics.avoid: Do not present a single rigid prescription, ignore individual differences, or treat an approximate alternative as evidence-identical.

mechanics.mechanic: Place a concise safety boundary near the first actionable recommendation, revisit it when discussing stronger versions, and identify conditions that warrant professional guidance or stopping.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use whenever a practical intervention has meaningful downside risk or a narrow margin between useful and harmful exposure.
mechanics.avoid: Do not bury warnings after persuasive benefits, use vague caution without actionable limits, or imply that motivation can override physiological danger.

mechanics.function: Closing loops through recap and callback
mechanics.mechanic: At transitions, restate the core model in compressed form, then use it to preview the next section or explain why the next evidence matters. This creates continuity across theory, research, and application.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use in long-form explanations with multiple studies, mechanisms, and recommendations.
mechanics.avoid: Do not repeat entire sections or introduce a recap that adds new unsupported claims.
